summary: 电影的诞生经历了几次不同的突破。光学玩具先让连续图像“动”起来，摄影和卷片让真实动作得以记录，银幕放映才让一群观众能同时看见它。
logic: 光学玩具如何制造运动错觉
摄影师怎样连续记录动作
卷片与早期电影摄影机
卢米埃尔兄弟把影片投上银幕
电影走向世界，开始讲述故事

paragraphs.role: 早期光学玩具和远见的持久性
paragraphs.brief: 动画的幻觉植根于两种光学现象：视觉的持久性和phi现象。
sentences: The illusion of moving pictures is rooted in two optical phenomena: persistence of vision and the phi phenomenon.
动画的幻觉植根于两种光学现象：视觉的持久性和phi现象。

Persistence of vision causes the human brain to briefly retain an image after it disappears, while the phi phenomenon creates an impression of continuous movement when images are shown in rapid succession.
视觉的持久性导致大脑在消失后短暂保留图像，而phi现象则给人一种连续快速显示图像时持续移动的印象。
sectionTitle: Early Optical Toys and the Persistence of Vision
早期光学玩具与视觉暂留

paragraphs.brief: 远在实际电影之前发明者就制造了好玩的装置来利用这些效果
sentences: Long before actual films, inventors built playful devices to exploit these effects.
远在实际电影之前发明者就制造了好玩的装置来利用这些效果

In the 1830s, devices like the phenakistoscope (1832), a spinning disc with sequential drawings viewed via slits and a mirror, and the zoetrope (1834), a rotating drum with slits cut into its sides, produced convincing illusions of motion from static images.
在1830年代，像phenakistoscope(1832年)这样的装置、一个通过剪切和镜子看的连续图画的旋转盘和一个侧面剪切的旋转鼓(1834年)产生了从静态图像中运动的令人信服的幻觉。
The zoetrope’s design—a cylinder with vertical slits and a strip of pictures on its inner wall—allowed multiple people to peer through the slits and see a “moving” scene as the drum spun.
Zoetrope的设计是垂直切割的圆筒，其内部墙上有一连串图片，让许多人通过裂缝看到一个 " 移动 " 的场景，就像鼓声一样。
These Victorian-era optical toys demonstrated the principles that make cinema possible.
这些维多利亚时代的光学玩具展示了使电影成为可能的原则。

paragraphs.brief: 与Zoetrope一样，它使用一个旋转圆柱内的一连串图片，但棱镜用一个内圆镜取代了Zoetorpe的狭窄的眼线。
sentences: In 1877, French inventor Charles-Émile Reynaud introduced the praxinoscope, an improved successor to the zoetrope.
1877年，法国发明家Charles-Émile Reynaud 介绍了磷基显像镜，这是Zoetrope的改进后继器。
Like the zoetrope, it used a strip of pictures inside a spinning cylinder, but the praxinoscope replaced the zoetrope’s narrow viewing slits with an inner circle of mirrors.
与Zoetrope一样，它使用一个旋转圆柱内的一连串图片，但棱镜用一个内圆镜取代了Zoetorpe的狭窄的眼线。
This clever modification meant a brighter, undistorted view of the images: as the wheel turned, a viewer looking into the mirrors saw a smooth animation without the dimming caused by slits.
这种巧妙的修改意味着对图像的更清晰、更清晰的视图：当方向盘转动时，一个看着镜子的观众看到一个平滑的动画，而没有被割断造成的模糊。
In essence, Reynaud’s 1877 praxinoscope was “similar to a zoetrope, with mirrors in place of viewing slits,” yielding a clearer picture of the moving drawings.
Reynaud的1877年的棱镜基本上 " 与Zoetrope相似，镜像取代了截肢，" 更清楚地描绘了移动图画。

paragraphs.brief: 这种光学发明——加上早先的魔术灯笼(一个17世纪的幻灯放映器)和Thaumatrope(1820年代的手动图像盘)——是电影的先锋，表明相继图像可以产生运动的幻觉。
sentences: Such optical inventions—along with the earlier magic lantern (a 17th-century projector for painted slides) and thaumatropes (hand-twisted picture disks from the 1820s)—were the precursors of cinema, demonstrating that sequential images could create the illusion of motion.
这种光学发明——加上早先的魔术灯笼(一个17世纪的幻灯放映器)和Thaumatrope(1820年代的手动图像盘)——是电影的先锋，表明相继图像可以产生运动的幻觉。

paragraphs.role: 摄影运动先锋(1870年代至1880年代)
paragraphs.brief: 到1870年代，摄影照射时间从一个小时降到了秒的一小部分，创新者开始实验系列摄影，快速拍摄照片以解剖运动。
sentences: Animation toys were limited to drawn images.
动画玩具仅限于绘画图像。
The next step toward cinema was capturing real motion.
进入电影院的下一个步骤是捕捉真正的运动。
This became possible with advances in photography.
随着摄影的进步，这成为可能。

By the 1870s, photographic exposure times had dropped from an hour to a fraction of a second, and innovators began experimenting with series photography—taking rapid sequences of pictures to dissect motion.
到1870年代，摄影照射时间从一个小时降到了秒的一小部分，创新者开始实验系列摄影，快速拍摄照片以解剖运动。
sectionTitle: 动态摄影的先驱（19 世纪 70 至 80 年代）

paragraphs.brief: 为了证明结果，Muybridge将图像安装在旋转盘上，用神奇的灯笼投射，在马的全速移动中制作了“动画”，这实际上发生在生活中。
sentences: One famous early experiment was conducted by English-born photographer Eadweard Muybridge.
由英国裔摄影师Eadweard Muybridge进行早期实验。
Beginning in 1872, Muybridge worked for Leland Stanford, a racehorse owner, to settle a debate: whether a galloping horse ever lifts all four hooves off the ground.
从1872年开始，Muybridge为赛马拥有者Leland Stanford工作，解决了一场辩论：一匹奔驰的马是否把四蹄都抬下地面。
Muybridge set up a row of cameras along a track, each triggered by the horse’s hooves as it passed.
穆伊布里奇沿着铁轨设置了一排摄像头每一个都由马的蹄子通过而触发
In 1877 he succeeded—the resulting photographs showed the horse fully airborne mid-gallop.
1877年，他成功成功—— 照片显示马完全在空中飘浮。

To demonstrate the result, Muybridge mounted the images on a rotating disk and projected them with a magic lantern, producing a “moving picture” of the horse at full gallop as it had actually occurred in life.
为了证明结果，Muybridge将图像安装在旋转盘上，用神奇的灯笼投射，在马的全速移动中制作了“动画”，这实际上发生在生活中。
This was a crucial proof-of-concept: real-life motion could be recorded and then played back as an animation.
这是一个关键的概念证明：现实生活运动可以被记录下来，然后作为动画回放。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然Marey的目标是科学的(分析动作太快，眼睛太快)，他只是短暂地试图放映他的图像，但他的工作进一步推进了电影所需的技术。
sentences: Meanwhile, in France, physiologist Étienne-Jules Marey devised a way to capture movement with a single camera.
与此同时，在法国，物理学家埃蒂安-朱利斯·马里设计了一种方法，用一台照相机来捕捉运动。
In 1882 Marey built the chronophotographic gun, a camera shaped like a rifle that could take 12 pictures per second of a moving subject (originally, birds in flight).
1882年，Marey制造了时速摄影枪，一个像步枪一样的照相机，每秒可以拍摄12张照片(原为飞行中的鸟类)。
Marey’s “gun” exposed images in rapid succession onto a rotating glass plate (later onto roll film).
Marey的 " 枪 " 将图像迅速传到一个旋转的玻璃板上(后到胶卷上)。
Although Marey’s goal was scientific (analyzing motion too fast for the eye) and he only briefly attempted to project his images, his work further advanced the techniques needed for motion pictures.
虽然Marey的目标是科学的(分析动作太快，眼睛太快)，他只是短暂地试图放映他的图像，但他的工作进一步推进了电影所需的技术。

paragraphs.brief: 到1880年代末期另一种关键成分就位了细胞胶卷胶卷
sentences: By the late 1880s, another key ingredient fell into place: celluloid roll film.
到1880年代末期另一种关键成分就位了细胞胶卷胶卷
Inventor Hannibal Goodwin conceived the idea of flexible film, and industrialist George Eastman began mass-producing photographic celluloid film in 1889.
发明家汉尼拔·古德温构想了灵活电影的概念，工业家乔治·伊斯特曼于1889年开始大规模制作摄影纤维素胶片。
Unlike glass plates or paper strips, the new celluloid film could hold thousands of images in a long, durable ribbon.
与玻璃板或纸条不同，新的纤维素胶片可以将数千张图像装在长长、耐久的丝带中。
This was crucial—it enabled the recording of extended sequences of photographs and thus the possibility of lengthy moving pictures, not just split-second motion studies.
这一点至关重要——它使得能够记录延长的相片序列，从而有可能进行冗长的移动图片，而不仅仅是分秒进行动作研究。

paragraphs.brief: 随着快速摄影和胶卷胶卷的提供，世界各地的发明家们匆忙忙忙忙着建造设备，以记录和展示移动中的照片。
sentences: With fast photography and roll film available, inventors around the world rushed to build devices to record and display moving pictures.
随着快速摄影和胶卷胶卷的提供，世界各地的发明家们匆忙忙忙忙着建造设备，以记录和展示移动中的照片。
An early breakthrough came from Louis Le Prince, a French-born inventor.
早期的突破来自于路易斯·勒普林斯一位法国出生的发明家
Le Prince created a single-lens motion picture camera in the late 1880s and managed to shoot several short films in Leeds, England.
1880年代后期勒普林斯制作了一部单镜头摄影机并在英国利兹拍摄了几部短片
Notably, in October 1888 he filmed Roundhay Garden Scene, a few seconds of moving imagery often cited as one of the first true motion pictures.
特别是1888年10月，他拍摄了 " 圆环花园场景 " 片段，几秒钟的动画往往被引用为第一批真正的电影之一。
By 1889 Le Prince was using Eastman’s new roll film in his camera.
1889年，Le Prince在他的相机中使用伊斯特曼的新胶卷。

He planned a public exhibition of his films in New York City in 1890— a demonstration that could have inaugurated the age of cinema—but fate intervened: Le Prince mysteriously disappeared in 1890 while traveling in France, and his film exhibition never took place.
他计划于1890年在纽约市举行电影公开展览——这次展览本可以为电影时代揭幕——但命运却干预了：1890年，Le Prince在法国旅行时神秘失踪，他的电影展览从未举行。
As a result, Le Prince’s contribution to cinema remained little known for decades.
因此，几十年来，勒普林斯对电影业的贡献鲜为人知。

paragraphs.brief: 1888年，他委托迪克森制作一部电影摄影机
sentences: In the end, credit for the first practical movie camera went to someone else.
最后，第一部实用电影摄像头的功劳转到了别人身上。

William Kennedy Laurie Dickson, a young Scottish engineer, was working in West Orange, New Jersey, at Thomas Edison’s laboratories, and he built what came to be widely regarded as the world’s first functional motion-picture camera.
威廉·肯尼迪·劳里·迪克森(William Kennedy Laurie Dickson)是一位年轻的苏格兰工程师，在新泽西州西奥兰治的托马斯·爱迪生实验室工作，他建造了被广泛认为是世界第一台运动图象摄影机。
Edison, already famous for his phonograph (invented in 1877), had envisioned adding visual marvels to his audio device.
Edison的录音机已经出名(1877年发明)，他设想给他的音频设备增添视觉奇迹。
In 1888 he tasked Dickson with developing a motion-picture camera.
1888年，他委托迪克森制作一部电影摄影机

paragraphs.brief: 迪克森在穆伊布里奇和马雷之前的工作基础上，综合了关键技术：一个快速停止的照相门(从时钟的脱落中改制)机制，以调节电影的间歇运动，以及穿孔的细胞胶片，以精确同步的方式推进图像。
sentences: Building upon the prior work of Muybridge and Marey, Dickson combined crucial technologies: a fast-stop camera shutter mechanism (adapted from a clock’s escapement) to regulate the intermittent motion of the film, and perforated celluloid film to advance images in precise synchronization.
迪克森在穆伊布里奇和马雷之前的工作基础上，综合了关键技术：一个快速停止的照相门(从时钟的脱落中改制)机制，以调节电影的间歇运动，以及穿孔的细胞胶片，以精确同步的方式推进图像。
By 1891, Dickson had succeeded in creating the Kinetograph camera, which could expose a rapid series of images onto the film strip.
到1891年，迪克森成功创建了Kinetagraphic相机，这可以将一系列快速图像暴露在电影条上。
The Kinetograph’s photographic system initially recorded about 50 feet of film running at roughly 40 frames per second—enough for a short sequence of action.
照片系统最初记录了大约50英尺的胶片，每秒大约40个框架，以进行短期动作。

paragraphs.role: Edison 的 Kinetoscope: 一部单视器动作片
paragraphs.brief: Thomas Edison对新媒体的态度与Le Prince公开展览的想法不同。
sentences: Thomas Edison’s approach to the new medium differed from Le Prince’s public exhibition idea.
Thomas Edison对新媒体的态度与Le Prince公开展览的想法不同。
Edison had originally conceived of motion pictures as a visual adjunct to his phonograph, something individuals could privately watch as they would listen to a record.
爱迪生最初把电影设计成影音片的副作用某些个人可以私下观看
Accordingly, after Dickson developed the camera, Edison did not immediately pursue a projector for large audiences.
因此，在迪克森开发了摄像机后，爱迪生没有立即为广大观众寻找投影机。
Instead, Dickson also designed a personal viewing device called the Kinetoscope, essentially a wooden cabinet peep-show machine.
相反，迪克森还设计了一个个人观看装置叫做Kinetoscope，基本上是木制的柜子观光机。
Inside each Kinetoscope, a continuous loop of film ran over a light source and shutter, and by peering through an eyepiece on top, a single viewer could watch the movie play.
每一台Kinetoscope里，一个连续的胶片环绕着一个光源和百叶窗，并且通过在顶部的一个眼镜的观察，一个观众可以看电影剧。
sectionTitle: Edison’s Kinetoscope: A One-Viewer Motion Picture
爱迪生的活动电影视镜：供一人观看的电影

paragraphs.brief: 爱迪生的第一个Kinetoscope客厅于1894年4月在纽约开业，展出一大批硬币操作机器，每个都向一个人一次展示一部短片。
sentences: Edison’s first Kinetoscope parlor opened in New York in April 1894, featuring banks of coin-operated machines—each showing a short film to one person at a time.
爱迪生的第一个Kinetoscope客厅于1894年4月在纽约开业，展出一大批硬币操作机器，每个都向一个人一次展示一部短片。
The Kinetoscope quickly became a commercial success; by 1894–95, Kinetoscope parlors and arcade installations were spreading across the U.S. and even overseas.
Kinetoscope很快成为商业成功；到1894-95年，Kinetoscools客厅和街机设施正在美国乃至海外蔓延。

To supply content, Edison’s team produced dozens of brief films (often simple scenes, vaudeville acts, or novelty performances) using a rudimentary studio called the Black Maria—a cramped, tar-paper shack on rails that could rotate to follow the sun for lighting.
为了提供内容，爱迪生的团队制作了数十部短片(通常是简单的场景、游荡的表演或新颖的表演)，使用一个叫“黑玛丽亚”的初级工作室，该工作室在铁轨上挤满了油布，可以绕着太阳转，以获得照明。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，Kinetoscope的设计有两个重大缺陷：电影短片，而且关键是，只有一个人可以一次观看节目。
sentences: However, the Kinetoscope’s design had two significant drawbacks: the films were short, and, crucially, only one person could view the show at a time.
然而，Kinetoscope的设计有两个重大缺陷：电影短片，而且关键是，只有一个人可以一次观看节目。
Despite Edison’s doubts about projection, other inventors saw that the real future of cinema lay in showing films to large audiences on a screen, rather than as solitary peepshows.
尽管爱迪生对投影有怀疑其他发明家认为电影的真正未来在于在屏幕上向广大观众展示电影而不是作为独家小看

paragraphs.brief: 值得注意的是，Edison也犯了一个战略错误，他忽略了为Kinetoscope系统取得外国专利。
sentences: Notably, Edison also made a strategic error—he neglected to secure foreign patents for the Kinetoscope system.
值得注意的是，Edison也犯了一个战略错误，他忽略了为Kinetoscope系统取得外国专利。
This allowed others in Europe to legally copy and modify his devices.
这使欧洲其他国家能够合法复制和修改他的装置。
By 1894, even as Edison’s machines proliferated, innovators abroad were already experimenting with improved motion-picture apparatus.
1894年，即使在爱迪生的机器扩散的同时，国外的创新者已经在试验改良的运动图象设备。
In London, for example, engineer William Friese-Greene and others had filed patents for projection devices and camera-projector hybrids around the same time.
例如，在伦敦，工程师威廉·弗里斯-格林和其他人就投影装置和摄影机-投影机混合器申请专利，时间大约在同一时间。
In Paris, a public demonstration of Edison’s Kinetoscope in 1894 inspired two brothers—Auguste and Louis Lumière—to take the final leap into projected cinema.
1894年在巴黎，爱迪生的Kinetoscope公开示威促使两个兄弟Auguste和Louis Lumière进入了电影放映的最后一步。

paragraphs.role: Lumière兄弟会和电影的诞生(1895年)
paragraphs.brief: 1895年初，路易斯和奥古斯特·卢米埃发明了他们的机器，他们称之为Cinématographe。
sentences: It was the Lumière brothers of France who ultimately gave the world the first true cinema experience.
是法国的鲁米埃兄弟最终给世界带来了第一次真正的电影体验。

Drawing on their background in photography (the Lumières were manufacturers of photographic plates), the brothers set out to develop a device that could record moving images and project them onto a screen for an audience.
他们利用摄影背景(Lumières是摄影板的制造商)，开始开发一个设备，可以记录移动图像并将其投放到观众屏幕上。
By early 1895, Louis and Auguste Lumière had invented their apparatus, which they named the Cinématographe.
1895年初，路易斯和奥古斯特·卢米埃发明了他们的机器，他们称之为Cinématographe。
sectionTitle: The Lumière Brothers and the Birth of Cinema (1895)
卢米埃尔兄弟与电影的诞生（1895 年）

paragraphs.brief: 这台创新机器约5公斤(11磅)，比爱迪生的相机小得多，更轻。爱迪生用电驱动的基内特仪用其重型发动机和电池重量超过200-300公斤(据说超过1,000磅)。
sentences: At roughly 5 kilograms (11 lbs), this innovative machine was much smaller and lighter than Edison’s cameras—Edison’s electrically driven Kinetograph had weighed in at over 200–300 kg (reportedly more than 1,000 lbs) with its heavy motor and batteries.
这台创新机器约5公斤(11磅)，比爱迪生的相机小得多，更轻。爱迪生用电驱动的基内特仪用其重型发动机和电池重量超过200-300公斤(据说超过1,000磅)。
In contrast, the Lumière Cinématographe was hand-cranked and portable, making location filming feasible.
相比之下，Lumière Cinématographe是手排和便携式的，因此可以拍摄地点。

Remarkably, the Cinématographe was a 3-in-1 device: it served as a camera for filming, could be used to print copies of the film, and, with a quick configuration change, became a projector to beam the motion pictures onto a screen.
尤其值得注意的是，Cinématographe是一个3英寸1的装置：它作为拍摄的相机，可以用来印刷影片的影印件，并且随着快速的配置变化，成为将运动图片传送到屏幕上的投影机。
(In fact, the word cinema derives from this invention’s name.)
(事实上，电影这个词来自这个发明的名称。)

paragraphs.brief: 1895年12月28日，Lumière兄弟在巴黎主办了一场具有里程碑意义的活动，这是世界首部商业公共电影放映。
sentences: On December 28, 1895, the Lumière brothers hosted a landmark event in Paris—the world’s first commercial public film screening.
1895年12月28日，Lumière兄弟在巴黎主办了一场具有里程碑意义的活动，这是世界首部商业公共电影放映。
Held at the Salon Indien du Grand Café in Paris, this demonstration is widely regarded as the birth of cinema as a commercial entertainment.
这次示威在巴黎大咖啡馆举行，被普遍认为是电影的诞生，是一种商业娱乐。

For the astonished paying audience, the Lumières projected a series of short films shot with their Cinématographe, including the famous Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory and Arrival of a Train at La Ciotat Station.
为了惊的受众，Lumières公司制作了一系列短片，包括著名的"工人离开Lumière工厂"和"火车抵达La Ciotat站".
The Cinématographe’s projected images of everyday life elicited gasps and applause; viewers marvelled at the realism of moving photographs coming to life on a screen.
电影画家对日常生活的投影图像引起了叹息和拍手；观众惊于电影上起的动画现实。
Unlike Edison’s one-person peepholes, here an entire room could share the same moving picture experience—an immersive spectacle that would quickly spread around the globe.
与爱迪生的独人尿片不同，这里整个房间可以分享同样的感人图片体验，即将迅速蔓延到全球的沉浸的景象。

paragraphs.brief: 卢米埃早期的电影主要是关于真实生活的纪录片：工人离开工厂、火车到达、人们在城市街道上走动。
sentences: The Lumières’ invention proved not only technically sound but also practical: “Unlike the Kinetograph, which was battery-driven and weighed over 1,000 pounds, the Cinématographe was hand-cranked, lightweight (less than 20 pounds), and relatively portable.”
卢米尔斯发明的技术不仅是实用的，而且是实用的："与电池驱动和重量超过1000磅的基内托格勒不同，基内托格雷夫是手动动的，轻量 (不到20磅)，相对便携式。
This portability had profound effects on the kinds of films made.
这种可移动性对制作的电影产生了深远的影响。
Edison’s heavy Kinetograph was mostly confined to a studio (hence his early films featured staged vaudeville acts or subjects that could perform in front of a stationary camera).
爱迪生的重水晶片大部分都局限在一个工作室(因此他早期的电影专门播放了舞台表演或可以在固定摄像机前表演的题材)。
The Lumière camera, by contrast, could be carried into the field.
对比之下，Lumière的照相机可以携带到现场。
Early Lumière films were largely documentary views (actualités) of real life: workers leaving a factory, trains arriving, people walking about in city streets.
卢米埃早期的电影主要是关于真实生活的纪录片：工人离开工厂、火车到达、人们在城市街道上走动。
These short snippets had little narrative but captured the motion of ordinary life in real environments—a novelty for audiences of the time.
这些短短的片段没有多少叙述，但捕捉到现实环境中的普通生活，这对当时的观众来说是新奇的。

paragraphs.brief: 卢米埃兄弟在第一次演出后几个月内开始向全世界派遣摄影师和摄影师小组。
sentences: Within months of their first show, the Lumière brothers began dispatching teams of cameramen-projectionists around the world.
卢米埃兄弟在第一次演出后几个月内开始向全世界派遣摄影师和摄影师小组。
These operators traveled to far-off places— from Moscow to New York, from India to Japan—filming local scenes and screening movies to enthralled audiences everywhere.
这些操作员从莫斯科到纽约，从印度到日本，前往遥远的地方拍摄当地景象，放映电影，让各地观众迷惑不解。

As one historian notes, “because the Lumières sent their cameramen all over the world in search of exotic subjects, the Cinématographe became the founding instrument of distant cinemas in Russia, Australia, and Japan.”
一位历史学家指出，“因为卢米埃派摄影师到世界各地寻找异国主题，西内马特摄影师成为俄罗斯、澳大利亚和日本遥远电影院的创始工具。”
In 1896, just a year after their first show, the Lumières opened theaters in London, New York, Brussels, and other cities to exhibit their growing catalog of films.
1896年，也就是他们第一次演出之后的一年，卢米耶尔人在伦敦、纽约、布鲁塞尔和其他城市开演了剧场，展出了他们不断增长的电影目录。

paragraphs.brief: Lumière的即时成功表明，电影不仅仅是一种过往的好奇。
sentences: The immediate success of the Lumière shows signaled that motion pictures were more than a passing curiosity.
Lumière的即时成功表明，电影不仅仅是一种过往的好奇。
What began as scientific experimentation and parlour entertainment had evolved into a new artistic and commercial medium.
科学实验和客厅娱乐活动已经演变成一个新的艺术和商业媒介
By 1896–1897, projected films (whether on Lumière machines or rival projectors) became a sensation across Europe and North America, often featured in music halls and vaudeville programs.
到1896-1897年，放映的电影(无论是在卢米埃机器上还是在竞争投影机上)成为欧洲和北美的感官，经常在音乐厅和游乐场节目中出现。

This period was sometimes called the “novelty period,” when the mere fact of moving images was the draw— theaters even advertised the machines (“Edison’s Vitascope” or “Lumière’s Cinématograph”) as the headline attraction.
这段时期有时被称为 " 新时期 "，当时，光是图画就吸引了感动图像，剧院甚至将机器( " 爱迪生的Vitascope " 或 " Lumière的Cinématograph " )作为头条新闻。
sectionTitle: 电影的全球传播与长远影响

paragraphs.brief: 但制片人很快开始扩展内容超越短视。
sentences: But filmmakers quickly started to extend content beyond short glimpses.
但制片人很快开始扩展内容超越短视。

Within a few years, pioneers like Georges Méliès in France and Edwin S. Porter in America were introducing storytelling, special effects, and editing to films, turning them from minute-long scenes into longer narratives by the early 1900s.
在几年内，法国的乔治·梅利埃和美国的埃德温·波特等先驱开始讲故事、发挥特效和编辑电影，在1900年代初期将它们从一小段场景变成较长的叙述。

paragraphs.brief: 电影最初是19世纪科学努力的产物，后来成为大众娱乐和交流的媒介——它将继续通过声音、颜色和范围不断演变，但总是植根于19世纪的“魔术”发明，这些发明首先给图片带来了生命。
sentences: In its infancy, cinema drew from existing traditions of photography, theater, and vaudeville, yet it rapidly developed a language of its own.
电影从现有的摄影、戏剧和游乐场传统中汲取了经验，然而电影迅速发展出一种自己的语言。
By the early 20th century, the “animated photographs” of the 1890s had transformed into a thriving film industry.
到20世纪初，1890年代的“动画片”已经转变为一个蓬勃发展的电影业。
As more people paid to see movies, investors built studios and dedicated movie theaters, and techniques improved for lighting, camera movement, and film editing.
随着更多的人花钱看电影，投资者建立了工作室和专门的电影院，并改进了照明、摄影机移动和电影编辑的技术。
What had started as a novelty of science became, in the new century, the world’s dominant form of mass entertainment.
在新世纪里，科学的新颖性成为世界大众娱乐的主要形式。

Originally a product of 19th-century scientific endeavor, cinema became a medium of mass entertainment and communication—one that would continue to evolve through sound, color, and beyond, but always rooted in those 19th-century “magic” inventions that first brought pictures to life.
电影最初是19世纪科学努力的产物，后来成为大众娱乐和交流的媒介——它将继续通过声音、颜色和范围不断演变，但总是植根于19世纪的“魔术”发明，这些发明首先给图片带来了生命。

points: 电影的诞生经历了几次不同的突破。光学玩具先让连续图像“动”起来，摄影和卷片让真实动作得以记录，银幕放映才让一群观众能同时看见它。
光学玩具制造运动错觉 → 摄影师连续记录现实动作 → 卷片与活动电影机延长画面 → 从单人窥视到公共放映
clauses: Persistence of vision causes the human brain to briefly retain an image after it disappears, ….
连接词 while 引出“while the phi phenomenon creates an impression of continuous movement when images are shown in rapid succession”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。

He planned a public exhibition of his films in New York City in 1890— a demonstration … —but fate intervened: Le Prince mysteriously disappeared in 1890 while traveling in France, and his film exhibition never took place.
“that could have inaugurated the age of cinema”修饰前面的 demonstration。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 demonstration，再把修饰信息接回主句。
